title: Implement MiFID II 'Cooling-Off Period' for High-Risk Trades
description: A new regulatory requirement under MiFID II mandates a 'cooling-off period' for certain classes of high-risk derivatives trades. This feature must be integrated into the PulseTrade Nexus platform. During this period, which must be configurable, the trade is held in a reversible 'pending' state, allowing for cancellation before it proceeds to final settlement. This task requires modifications across multiple microservices to handle the new trade lifecycle state, orchestrate the time-delayed settlement, and ensure compliance.

project_spec.name: PulseTrade Nexus
project_spec.description:
PulseTrade Nexus is an expert-level fintech trading platform engineered specifically for the healthcare sector. It enables hospital groups, insurers, and pharmaceutical distributors to execute, settle, and audit multi-currency supply-chain and treatment-based financial transactions while ensuring end-to-end regulatory compliance (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, PSD2). Leveraging a healthcare-centric taxonomy, every trade is coupled with clinical context— such as procedure codes, drug identifiers, or episodes of care— allowing Risk & Compliance teams to correlate financial flows with actual patient events for real-time fraud detection, granular audit trails, and richer revenue-cycle analytics.

The solution is delivered as 94 loosely coupled microservices organised around a strict hexagonal architecture. Each service exposes an inbound healthcare-aware Port (gRPC/REST or message topic) and delegates business logic to a Core that is fully agnostic of transport, storage, or cryptography. Outbound Adapters implement connection to EMR/EHR systems, KYC services, clearing houses, payment gateways, or on-prem clinical data lakes. Event Sourcing and CQRS capture every state transition as an immutable clinical-financial event, while Saga orchestration coordinates multi-currency settlement flows across pharmacies, insurers, and providers. Security-by-Design principles pervade the codebase: transparent AES-GCM encryption of PHI payloads, attribute-based access control, runtime integrity checks, and continuous compliance reporting that maps trades back to clinical consent artifacts.
dependencies: libgrpc-c (gRPC for C, used for Ports & inter-service communication)
protobuf-c (schema-first message contracts for CQRS commands/events)
OpenSSL 3.x (TLS 1.3, AES-GCM, X.509 mutual auth, envelope encryption)
libpq / PostgreSQL 15 (transaction store, event-sourcing ledger, time-series)
Apache Kafka + librdkafka (domain event bus, outbox, Saga orchestration)
libjansson (JSON serialization for REST adapters and compliance exports)
libcurl (HTTP/REST adapters to external KYC/FHIR APIs)
libsodium (high-level crypto primitives, sealed boxes for secret rotation)
CMocka (unit testing ports & cores in isolation)
Prometheus C client + OpenTelemetry C SDK (observability, audit trail hooks)
